Chapter 2: The Struggle to Balance Obsession and Everyday Life
So, what happens when the excitement of a big project wears off, and it starts blending into your daily grind? Suddenly, it’s not just about reading anymore—it’s about squeezing this huge commitment into a life that’s already packed with work, family, and all those little distractions we never see coming.
The encyclopedia started out as a curiosity, but pretty soon, it demanded time and attention—more than I expected. And, honestly, something else had to give.
At work, the project felt like a secret superpower—and, sometimes, a bit of a curse. I’d be in a meeting, tempted to casually drop some obscure fact I’d just learned. Every now and then, it landed perfectly—a quirky story about the origin of a word or a forgotten inventor, and suddenly, I seemed like the most interesting person in the room. But more often? People just rolled their eyes, and the conversation would grind to a halt. There’s a thin line between being fascinating and being, well, a bit much.
Things at home got even trickier. At first, my partner thought the whole thing was fun—even charming. But as the months rolled by, dinner conversations slowly turned into trivia battles, and evenings we used to spend together were now all about chasing down the next volume. We started arguing about priorities: was the pursuit of knowledge more important than our relationship? It was easy to lose perspective, to forget that learning is supposed to make life richer—not take it over.
Friends reacted in all sorts of ways. Some were entertained, treating my obsession as a quirky personality trait. Others got annoyed, maybe feeling like they couldn’t keep up or like they’d been left out. There were still great moments—late-night debates, laughing together over the weirdest facts—but there were also times when I felt totally alone. No matter how hard I tried, this project was a solitary road, and it was tough to bring anyone else along for the ride.
Eventually, I realized the encyclopedia itself was a perfect metaphor for what I was going through. Every new volume was a fresh challenge—every entry, a test of patience. Some days, the words just blurred together and the facts didn’t mean much. But then, I’d stumble on something amazing—a story about a forgotten explorer, or a strange link between two totally random things—and suddenly, it all felt worth it. Those tiny sparks of wonder made the struggle bearable, even when the rest of my life felt like it was coming undone.
Here’s the thing: obsession always comes with a cost. Chasing knowledge can be thrilling, but it can also leave you feeling isolated. Relationships take a back seat, work feels more like an obligation, and the joy of learning gets buried under the weight of “just getting it done.” It’s way too easy to let a passion turn into a burden—to lose sight of why you started in the first place.
But there’s a lesson in all of this—a reminder to be resilient. This project forced me to rethink my priorities and figure out how to keep my balance. Reading just for the sake of reading wasn’t enough. I needed to weave what I learned into my life, to share it, and to use it to connect with others—not to build walls around myself. The encyclopedia was supposed to be a tool, not a master.
And maybe, the real challenge was never about finishing the project at all—it was about finding a way to let curiosity and life coexist.
